name: Vikos-Aoös National Park
blurb: Gorge cliffs, oak woods, chamois, wolves and brown bears in the Pindus.

tip.title: Remove the wolf
tip.text: Set Gray wolf to -100% and watch chamois, roe deer and wild boar numbers rise, then pressure on oaks and mountain grasses, and less carrion for ravens.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Kermes oak & oaks
nodes.desc: Oaks, including kermes oak recorded near the site, are common in the sub-Mediterranean woodland and drop acorns that many animals eat.

nodes.name: Mountain grasslands
nodes.desc: Grasses of the subalpine meadows above about 1,500 m, where chamois graze in summer.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A rare goat-antelope of the gorge cliffs. It eats highland grasses and herbs in summer and moves lower in winter.
A small woodland deer that browses leaves, shoots and herbs. It is recorded in the area.
An omnivore that roots for acorns, plants and invertebrates in the woods.
A tree-climbing rodent that eats nuts, seeds and fruit and is prey of foxes and martens.
A woodland crow well known for gathering and caching acorns.
A versatile hunter of small mammals, birds and lizards, also eating fruit and carrion.
A nocturnal mustelid that hunts rodents and birds and also eats fruit.
An intelligent scavenger that feeds on carrion, including kills left by wolves.
A pack hunter of wild ungulates such as chamois, roe deer and boar. It is listed among the large carnivores of the site.
Mostly a plant eater, taking acorns, berries and grasses, with meat and carrion in spring. The site is among its last southern European strongholds.
Summer sun drives growth on the sunny slopes and the high meadows.
Rain and meltwater feed the woods and meadows, but the limestone drains fast so surface water is scarce.
Snow covers the high meadows and pushes chamois down to lower forest in winter.
Thin soils over limestone, where water drains underground through caves and cracks.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

story: Vikos-Aos National Park spans 12,600 hectares of mountainous terrain in the region of Epirus in northwestern Greece, featuring deep canyons and dense forests. Founded in 1973, it is home to a rich variety of flora and large mammals like the brown bear.
matters: The park is part of the Natura 2000 ecological network and a UNESCO Geopark, serving as one of the last European strongholds for the brown bear and providing a valuable habitat for nature conservation in Greece.
